evals.prompt: My teammate sent me this draw.io file but I've never used draw.io and I'm new to system design. Can you explain what this system does? The file is /Users/trang_thi_thuy.n/GIT/ntttrang-plugin/skills/drawio-understand-workspace/fixtures/architecture.drawio
evals.expected_output: A beginner-friendly Markdown system map: plain-language summary, node/boundary/edge inventory covering swimlanes (Client/Server), the database cylinders, the dashed 'validates token' edge, a step-by-step flow walkthrough, and a Mermaid recreation
assertions: Decoded the compressed .drawio file and identified all 7 nodes: User, Browser, CDN, API Gateway, Auth Service, Main DB, Redis Cache
Identifies the two swimlanes (Client and Server) and explains them as boundaries / responsibility areas
Recognizes Main DB and Redis Cache as data stores (cylinder/database shapes)
Explains the dashed 'validates token' edge from API Gateway to Auth Service, noting dashed styling
Includes a numbered step-by-step walkthrough of the request flow
Includes a Mermaid diagram recreating the flow

evals.prompt: i'm a junior dev and this is the checkout flow our team drew in draw.io. walk me through what happens step by step, including the error paths. /Users/trang_thi_thuy.n/GIT/ntttrang-plugin/skills/drawio-understand-workspace/fixtures/checkout-flow.drawio.xml
evals.expected_output: Markdown explanation that follows the main happy path through the decision diamonds (Logged in?, Items in stock?, Payment approved?) and narrates each branch including the retry loop and backorder path, in beginner-friendly language
assertions: Identifies all three decision points: 'Logged in?', 'Items in stock?', 'Payment approved?'
Narrates the main happy path in order from 'Customer clicks Checkout' to 'Order complete'
Explains the payment-failure retry loop (payment error -> retry -> re-enter payment details)
Explains the backorder branch when items are not in stock
Uses beginner-friendly language: explains or avoids unexplained jargon
Structure is scannable: summary + inventory + step-by-step walkthrough (tables or lists), not one wall of prose
